newsitem.title: USA: IMM currencies end mostly higher, yen down slightly.
newsitem.headline: IMM currencies end mostly higher, yen down slightly.

text.p: IMM currency futures ended mostly higher, with yen settling slightly lower on expectations Japan's Ministry of Finance (MOF) would suspend almost all operations at Hanwa Bank Ltd, traders and analysts said.
After the market closed, MOF announced it would order Hanwa to suspend most of its business. A source said the Bank of Japan (BOJ) set up an emergency fund to prevent a crisis at Hanwa Bank.
The lingering bank problems in Japan suggested to most traders that Japan was not in the position to raise rates.
December yen fell to $0.008983 as the dollar rose above 111.70 spot yen. The contract is expected to test the next support level at $0.008961, or 112.00 spot, they said.
The yen came under even more pressure against Canadian and Australian dollars, which was reflected in December currency futures contracts.

December Australian dollars rose above resistance at $0.7980 after finding follow-through buying from overnight trade. One Swiss fund was a heavy buyer of Aussie dollars, as well as a good buyer of mark/Swiss francs. December Australian dollars rose to $0.8012 in light pit trade.
December Canadian dollars, meanwhile, climbed to $0.7482 and are seen rising to $0.7500 in the near term.
While traders began to fade out expectations for a rate hike in Japan, forecasts that the Bundesbank would not lower German interest rates strengthened.
Both the German M3 money supply data and the German Ifo business confidence index indicated the economy was picking up steam, and eroded beliefs the Bundesbank would lower interest rates.
December marks rose above $0.6700, as the dollar/mark slipped below 1.4950 spot.
The next key resistance level for December marks is at $0.6745, or 1.4850 spot, and $0.7933, or 1.2640 spot.
"If December marks really take off that could spook people holding long dollar/Swiss franc positions," a currency trader said.

At the end of pit trade, December yen was off $0.000003 at $0.008991, marks were up $0.0038 at $0.6690, Swiss francs were up $0.0027 at $0.7915, sterling was up $0.0048 at $1.6796, Canadian dollars rose $0.0010 at $0.7479, Australian dollars rallied $0.0069 to $0.8010 and pesos were up $0.000050 at $0.124550.
